anchors.title: Adopting the Artificial Intelligence Governance Framework and Creating the National Artificial Intelligence Council
anchors.verified_via: Aureada CPA Law explainer (2026-11-14) + Official Gazette references + press (2026-11-14/19); obligations mapped in modules/gov/COMPLIANCE_EO131_MATRIX.md
anchors.notes: Four framework elements; NAIC chaired by Executive Secretary, vice-chaired by DEPDev; DEPDev is Secretariat; five TWGs (Institutions; Data & R&D; Capabilities; Infrastructure; Demand Generation). s.5: DICT runs the digital monitoring & reporting platform, agencies update it QUARTERLY, Council reports to the President within 30 days of each quarter's end. s.6: framework review at least biennially. s.8: interim Secretariat within 30 days of effectivity. No penal clause; sector regulators keep their mandates; LGUs/private sector encouraged (not bound).

anchors.title: Principles for the Ethical and Responsible Development, Deployment, and Use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in the Government
anchors.verified_via: Cruz Marcelo & Tenefrancia client alert (fetched 2026-11-23, full principles list + committee composition)
anchors.notes: Applies to ALL government officials/employees incl. GOCCs with original charters, LGUs, SUCs. Ten principles: Proportionality & Do No Harm; Human-centricity; Fairness & Non-discrimination; Transparency & Explainability; Data Governance, Privacy & Protection; Responsibility & Accountability; Multistakeholder & Adaptive Governance & Collaboration; Cyber Safety & Security; Robustness & Reliability; Sustainability. Every covered agency using AI: internal committee at minimum of IT + Legal unit reps + AI developer rep + AI deployer rep, recommending allowable extent to the Head of Agency. Governance requirements flow into ISSPs, procurement, technical specs, ToRs, service agreements. Affected persons may contest AI-assisted decisions and request human review. DICT+CSC joint implementing guidelines due within 90 days of effectivity (~2026-09-07) — OWED: verify whether issued (audit watch W-1).

anchors.title: Responsible AI use in preparing GAD plans and budgets
Foundational Guidelines on Artificial Intelligence in Basic Education
anchors.verified_via: Original scan held + human-corrected transcription (DO_s2026_003r-1.md); machine-readable set produced 2026-11-23
anchors.notes: s.1.4 Digital Maturity Assessment (Annex C) before school AI deployment; s.1.5 contractual warranties: no training on DepEd data for commercial use, content provenance/watermarking enabled, 72-hour breach incident reporting; s.1.6 PIA before deployment (DPO-facilitated; parental consent mandatory for learners under 18); s.1.7 DepEd AI Registry — register every AI system BEFORE use (name, vendor, purpose + risk classification, PIA results, responsible officers, conformity assessment); s.1.8 registry = official monitoring/transparency reference. Annex A: three AI-use declaration templates (personnel/teacher/learner, prompts listed). Annex B: four risk tiers x three stakeholder groups (unacceptable prohibited; high-risk requires PIA+HITL+audit logging+appeal; limited requires disclosure; minimal standard IT controls). Annex D: PIA guide. Annex E: 11-column registry with worked rows (ChatGPT/Copilot/Gemini as pilots) naming ISO/IEC 23894 + NIST AI RMF as the conformity references.

anchors.title: Policies, Standards, and Guidelines for the Framework on Artificial Intelligence (AI) in Higher Education

effective.effectivity: 15 days after publication + administrative registry filing

anchors.verified_via: Original scan held + human-corrected transcription produced 2026-11-23 (10 pp, OCR+proof); official URL confirmed live
anchors.notes: Applies to ALL public and private HEIs under CHED jurisdiction (press coverage Sep-Oct 2026: ~2,366 HEIs). Art.II defines High-Risk AI Systems (grading decisions, admissions screening, faculty evaluation tools, proctoring, scholarship eligibility; HEIs may add) and Meaningful Human Review. Art.IV s.3 seven declarations. Art.V principles 1-8 incl. tiered impact assessment (minimal/moderate/high-impact) and 'no AI system should autonomously determine academic outcomes without meaningful human review'. Art.VII Pillar 1 s.7-9 (human agency; disclosure required, HEI-defined, CHED provides model templates — NOT YET PUBLISHED as of 2026-11-23, gap-fill opportunity; AI detection tools never the sole basis for misconduct findings). Pillar 3 s.14: ANY HEI deploying high-risk AI systems SHALL establish an Institutional AI Governance Framework defining internal oversight and approval pathways; s.15 enhanced safeguards; s.16 CHED model risk framework (adopt-and-adapt, no rigid national taxonomy); s.17 oversight pathways; s.18 four explicit non-obligations (no universal AI detection, no full-documentation mandate, no one-size governance structure, no mandatory AI regulatory center). Art.VIII phased rollout. Art.X s.30 transition 12 months default (18-24 where readiness warrants).

anchors.title: Governance Principles for the Use of Artificial Intelligence in Financial Services (STARS)
anchors.official_url: https://www.bsp.gov.ph/Regulations/Issuances/2026/ (M-2026-031; related M-2026-034 PDF confirmed at /M-2026-034.pdf — fetch both, verify which carries STARS)
anchors.verified_via: Quisumbing Torres / Baker McKenzie alert (2026-07-20) + DataGuidance (2026-08-03) + BSP memo PDF (M-2026-034) surfaced in search
anchors.notes: STARS = Sustainability, Transparency, Accountability, Responsibility, Security (five principles). Voluntary supervisory expectations, proportionate to institution size/complexity. Expects: centralized AI inventories, independent model validation, board oversight, documentation sufficient for BSP review. Vendors stay accountable to the bank. Related: BSP Circular 1160 (digital financial consumer protection).
